A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GaussianSpa. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including content moved into v3's supplementary material.

before.justification: v2 reports original GaussianSpa rendering results on three benchmarks, along with convergence, sparsity, and visual analyses in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results and accompanying analyses, including per-scene results and visual comparisons in its supplementary material.

M1.justification: The opacity sparsity constraint, alternating optimizing and sparsifying steps, top-k projection, multiplier update, and final tuning procedure are unchanged. Consolidating the methodological remarks does not introduce a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same novel-view-synthesis task on Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks&Temples, and Deep Blending, with the same thirteen scenes. No new dataset, domain, or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparator rows, including both LP-3DGS variants. LightGaussian remains in the corresponding visual and curve comparisons, and Table 2 retains EfficientGS and LightGaussian. The relocated carpet comparison still includes Mini-Splatting.

E3.justification: Both versions specify the same starting checkpoints, initiation of optimizing-sparsifying at 15K iterations, and Gaussian removal at 25K. Evaluation metrics and the reported sparsity-penalty and update-interval settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The penalty/interval convergence analysis and Figure 9 move to the supplementary material. Reduction-rate analyses, alternative importance-criterion experiments, and visual case studies are retained; the carpet ellipsoid comparison becomes supplementary Figure 12.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. Dataset averages and curves retain the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: All five matched tables contain identical numerical results after accounting for renumbering. For example, GaussianSpa retains 27.85 dB PSNR with 0.547 million Gaussians on Mip-NeRF 360. The matched curves and visual comparisons retain their findings.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the rationale for reformulating Equation 5: v2 attributes the difficulty to Gaussians being continuous functions rather than differentiable variables, whereas v3 identifies the nondifferentiable count constraint. Equations 1–17 and the subsequent projection derivation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same optimization-based simplification contribution and quality-versus-compactness claims, including approximately 0.9 dB improvement with tenfold fewer Gaussians on Deep Blending.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly attributes mask-based pruning failures to weak sparsity enforcement and acknowledges that these methods impose sparsity through mask losses. The existing interpretations concerning information preservation, adaptive Gaussian density, and compression compatibility remain.

D1.justification: v3 removes the explicit Section 3.3 statement that gradients are not calculated for z and the multiplier, together with its training-overhead explanation. Hardware, checkpoint information, training milestones, and the project-page address remain unchanged. This is reduced documentation, not evidence of an implementation change.

R1.justification: v3 removes the TensorFlow, Mip-NeRF (2021), and Zip-NeRF references. It also distinguishes quantization generally from vector quantization and refines its positioning against mask-based pruning. The principal compression-method and optimization relationships remain.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, and optimization discussion undergo substantial condensation and rewriting. Three methodological remarks become one, convergence discussion moves into a new supplementary discussion section, and the appendix is reorganized as supplementary material.

P2.justification: The displays are substantially reorganized: Figure 6 is split between the main text and supplementary Figure 12; Figure 9 and Table 2 move to the supplement; the visual-example and opacity figures exchange numbering; per-scene tables are rearranged; and Figure 7 is restyled. These changes principally redisplay existing evidence.

improvement.justification: v3 improves explanatory precision about the nondifferentiable count constraint and reduces repetition in the methodological remarks and related-work discussion while retaining the empirical evidence. These clarity gains are partly offset by removing the explicit auxiliary-gradient and overhead explanation. The resulting improvement is limited; the method, numerical results, and empirical support remain stable.
